chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

If a man experiences a wet dream and semen comes onto his garment, then he should wash the part that it reached. But if he thinks that semen reached it, yet is not certain, and he does not see its place, then he should sprinkle it with water. And if he is certain that it has reached it, but he does not see its place, then he should wash his entire garment, for that is better.

key_terms.فَلْيَغْسِلِ: he should wash as a legal act of purification
key_terms.فَلْيَنْضِحْهُ: he should sprinkle it with water
key_terms.مَنِيٌّ: semen causing ritual impurity on the garment
key_terms.يَسْتَيْقِنْ: to become certain or fully sure

ai.seo_question: What should be done if semen gets on clothing after a wet dream and its exact place is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the purification of clothing from semen after a wet dream. It distinguishes between certainty and mere suspicion, instructing washing of the affected area when known, sprinkling water when uncertain, and washing the whole garment when certain of impurity but unable to locate it.
